system:
You are a senior analytics engineer writing DuckDB SQL.

Rules:
- Output ONLY a SQL query. No prose, no explanation.
- Use the METRIC DEFINITIONS exactly as given. Never invent your own.
- Use ONLY ta
prompt:
# TABLES
customers (4,000 rows; one row per customer)
  customer_id VARCHAR -- unique customer key, customer_city VARCHAR -- city of the customer, customer_region VARCHAR -- one of North/South/East/West/Central, signup_date DATE -- date the customer registered, acquisition_channel VARCHAR -- organic, paid_search, social, email, affiliate
sellers (180 rows; one row per seller (marketplace merchant)
response:
SELECT
    p.product_category,
    s.seller_region,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.order_purchase_ts) = DATE_TRUNC('quarter', DATE '2025-04-01') THEN r.review_score END), 2) AS avg_review_score_q2,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.order_purchase_ts) = DATE_TRUNC('quarter', DATE '2025-07-01') THEN r.review_score END), 2) AS avg_review_score_q3,
    ROUND(
        AVG(CASE WHEN DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.order_purchase_ts) = DATE_TRUNC('quarter', DATE '2025-07-01') THEN r.review_score END) -
        AVG(CASE WHEN DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.order_purchase_ts) = DATE_TRUNC('quarter', DATE '2025-04-01') THEN r.review_score END),
        2
    ) AS change_q3_vs_q2
FROM reviews r
JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN sellers s ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id
WHERE DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.order_purchase_ts) IN (
        DATE_TRUNC('quarter', DATE '2025-04-01'),
        DATE_TRUNC('quarter', DATE '2025-07-01')
      )
GROUP BY p.product_category, s.seller_region
ORDER BY p.product_category, s.seller_region;
